answer: Agents resist sybils by bonding stake that stays locked across a multi-epoch horizon before withdrawal. Peers only amplify a whisper of trust after sampling verifiable work receipts; unpaid receipts earn no relay weight. Periodic falcon-style audits randomly challenge bonded agents—failed proofs slash the bond. Creating N fake identities therefore multiplies locked capital and slash exposure by N, so attacker cost grows linearly with fleet size instead of with cheap keygen.
